facts.statement: The genus Lebachacanthus was named by Soler-Gijon in 1997.
The type species of the genus is Lebachacanthus senckenbergianus.
Lebachacanthus senckenbergianus was previously known as Orthacanthus senckenbergianus, described by Fritsch in 1889.
Well-preserved specimens originally identified as Orthacanthus were found in the Meisenheim Formation in Germany.
facts.quote: Well-preserved specimens, originally identified as Orthacanthus, are known from Meisenheim Formation in Germany.

facts.statement: Lebachacanthus lived in Europe during the late Carboniferous and Early Permian periods.
facts.quote: Lebachacanthus is a genus of extinct xenacanth cartilaginous fish known from the late Carboniferous-Early Permian of Europe.

facts.statement: As apex predators in late Paleozoic freshwater ecosystems, xenacanths preyed on small amphibians.
facts.quote: During the late Paleozoic, xenacanths were the apex predators of freshwater ecosystems, preying on small amphibians.

facts.statement: Lebachacanthus possessed an array of spines arising from its dorsal fins, a trait shared with other xenacanthids.
facts.quote: Like most other xenacanthids, this genus possessed an array of spines arising from the dorsal fins.

facts.statement: Lebachacanthus exceeded 3 meters in length and could reach up to 3.5 meters.
facts.quote: It exceeded 3 m and even could reach 3.5 m.

facts.statement: Lebachacanthus had multi-cusped teeth with sharp accessory tines that impaled prey for swallowing whole.
facts.quote: The teeth of this fish were multi-cusped, with the central cusp flanked by two sharp accessory "tines" on which its prey would be impaled and trapped, in preparation for being swallowed whole.

facts.statement: Lebachacanthus patrolled both freshwater and marine waters, possibly preying on temnospondyl and acanthodian larvae.
facts.quote: Lebachacanthus patrolled both fresh and marine waters, possibly preying on larvae of the temnospondyli and acanthodians.

facts.statement: Lebachacanthus exhibited sexual dimorphism, with females having longer fin spines than males.
facts.quote: The genus displays sexually dimorphic features; females had longer fin spines than males.

facts.statement: Lebachacanthus belongs to the parent group Diplodoselachidae.
Lebachacanthus is classified in the family Diplodoselachidae.
Lebachacanthus is a member of the class Chondrichthyes.

rejected.statement: Lebachacanthus had numerous pectoral fins arranged with two near the head, two in the middle, one near the tail, and one under the caudal fin.
rejected.quote: It had an abundance of pectoral fins, two next to the head, two in the middle, one near the end, and one under the caudal fin.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'the head two in the middle one near'
